steps.title: Collect and sterilize eggs
steps.instruction: Gently squeeze eggs from females into sterile 20 mm or 60 mm petri dishes, cover, and transfer to the dissection area; clean the dissection surface with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Euthanize male and harvest testes
steps.instruction: Euthanize the male in freshly made, filter‑sterilized tricaine/MS‑222 buffered with sodium bicarbonate, spray the outside of the euthanized male with 70 % ethanol and wipe with a Kimwipe or paper towel; dissect testes by cutting from next to the anal vent to the jaw, push the intestine aside, remove testes with sterile forceps, and transfer testes to the top of a sterile petri dish.

steps.title: Macerate testes
steps.instruction: Using a clean new razor, make lengthwise and cross cuts to macerate the collected testes.

steps.title: Mix testes with antibiotic medium
steps.instruction: Add 5–10 drops of filter‑sterilized antibiotic stickleback medium to the macerated testes with a sterile transfer pipette, pipette up and down until the solution is cloudy; transfer 3–5 drops of this mixture to each clutch of stickleback eggs (one set of testes can fertilize up to three clutches).

steps.title: Incubate eggs with sperm
steps.instruction: Incubate the eggs with sperm for 15 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Cover eggs with antibiotic medium and rinse
steps.instruction: Add filter‑sterilized antibiotic stickleback medium to the fertilized eggs to fully cover them; transfer fertilized eggs to sterile 100 mm petri dishes and rinse in approximately 100 mL sterile antibiotic stickleback medium.

steps.title: Incubate fertilized eggs to early stage
steps.instruction: Incubate fertilized eggs at 20–23 °C until they reach the 2–8 cell stage (~2 hours post‑fertilization).

steps.title: Remove non‑viable embryos and rinse
steps.instruction: Using a sterile transfer pipette, remove non‑viable embryos and egg goo; separate viable eggs gently with sterile tweezers or paintbrushes; rinse viable embryos twice with fresh antibiotic stickleback medium.

steps.title: Transfer embryos to sterile beakers
steps.instruction: At ~6 hours post‑fertilization, place ~100 viable embryos into sterile autoclaved 50 mL beakers with foil tops; add approximately 40 mL filter‑sterilized stickleback medium to each beaker.

steps.title: Prepare equipment and hood
steps.instruction: Clean the following items with 70 % ethanol and keep them inside the hood: three sterile 50 mL beakers with foil tops, individually wrapped sterile transfer pipettes or 2 mL pipettes, 1 L filter‑sterilized stickleback medium, 0.003 % bleach, 0.2–0.4 % PVP‑I solution, and a large beaker for waste. Turn UV light off, spray the outside of each beaker with 70 % ethanol (avoid ethanol entering the beaker), then bring embryos into the hood.

steps.title: First medium exchange
steps.instruction: Transfer embryos to a clean autoclaved foil‑covered beaker; carefully pour off all but ~10 mL stickleback medium into a waste container; transfer the remaining ~10 mL medium with embryos into a clean 50 mL beaker; add ~20 mL sterile stickleback medium to the original beaker to recover any remaining eggs; combine all eggs in the new beaker and bring the total volume to 50 mL with sterile stickleback medium.

steps.title: Wash embryos three times
steps.instruction: Rinse embryos three times with 50 mL filter‑sterilized stickleback medium.

steps.title: Disinfect embryos with PVP‑I
steps.instruction: Immerse embryos in ~50 mL 0.2–0.4 % PVP‑I solution for 10 minutes; rinse once with sterile stickleback medium; transfer embryos to a fresh beaker as described in the medium‑exchange step; rinse embryos an additional two times with sterile stickleback medium.

steps.title: Disinfect embryos with bleach
steps.instruction: Immerse embryos in 50 mL 0.003 % bleach for 10 minutes; rinse once with sterile stickleback medium; transfer embryos to a fresh beaker as described in the medium‑exchange step; rinse embryos an additional two times with sterile stickleback medium.

steps.title: Transfer embryos to sterile flasks
steps.instruction: Using sterile individually wrapped pipettes, transfer embryos to sterile tissue‑culture flasks containing sterile stickleback medium: 25 cm² flasks – up to 10 eggs, 75 cm² – up to 20 eggs, 150 cm² – up to 40 eggs, 300 cm² – up to 80 eggs; tightly close flasks.

steps.title: Add medium to flasks
steps.instruction: Add sterile stickleback medium to each flask: 25 cm² – 19 mL (≈1 mL used for transfer), 75 cm² – 48 mL (≈2 mL transfer), 150 cm² – 96 mL (≈4 mL transfer), 300 cm² – 194 mL (≈6 mL transfer).

steps.title: Incubate embryos in controlled conditions
steps.instruction: Place flasks flat in a light‑controlled incubator at 18–20 °C; ensure eggs do not enter the neck of the flask.

steps.title: Maintain germ‑free fish
steps.instruction: Keep fish in germ‑free flasks up to 14 days post‑fertilization without food; after 14 days provide food.

steps.title: Record daily fish viability
steps.instruction: Each day, record the number of fish that are dead or unresponsive to external stimuli; keep flasks upright and verify no eggs are in the neck.

steps.title: Plate water for microbial growth
steps.instruction: Plate 50–100 µL of water onto TSA plates and incubate at 20 °C; growth indicates contamination.

steps.title: Microscopy check for flask contamination
steps.instruction: Examine the bottom interior of each flask with an inverted light microscope at ≥40× magnification; presence of cocci, rods, or filamentous microbes indicates contamination.

steps.title: 16S PCR assay for contamination
steps.instruction: Collect 0.22 µm‑filtered water, extract DNA from the filter, and perform PCR of the 16S rRNA gene using primers 27F and 1492R; a ~1400 bp band on gel indicates contamination.

steps.title: UV‑sterilize reusable items
steps.instruction: Expose all reusable items (beakers, pipettes, etc.) to UV light for a minimum of 10 minutes.

steps.title: Sterilize dissecting tools
steps.instruction: Rinse scissors and forceps briefly in 10 % bleach, then rinse in 70 % ethanol.
